title: Filter affordable cards
prompt: Define affordable(cards, elixir) using a list comprehension to return names whose cost <= elixir, in input order. Example: Xbow at 6 is excluded when elixir is 5.
tests:
cards = [{"name":"Xbow","cost":6},{"name":"Skeletons","cost":1}]
assert affordable(cards,5) == ["Skeletons"], "only Skeletons fits five elixir"
assert affordable(cards,6) == ["Xbow","Skeletons"], "include exact-cost cards in input order"
hint: Put the expression before for and the condition after the loop.
solution:
def affordable(cards, elixir):
    return [card["name"] for card in cards if card["cost"] <= elixir]

title: Rank recorded losses
prompt: Define rank_losses(counts), returning card names ordered by decreasing count, then alphabetically for ties. Example: {"Xbow":2,"Giant":2,"Knight":1} gives ["Giant","Xbow","Knight"].
tests:
assert rank_losses({"Xbow":2,"Giant":2,"Knight":1}) == ["Giant","Xbow","Knight"], "sort counts descending and tied names ascending"
assert rank_losses({}) == [], "empty counts should produce no names"
hint: A tuple (-counts[name], name) orders first by the negative count.
solution:
def rank_losses(counts):
    return sorted(counts, key=lambda name: (-counts[name], name))

title: Number paired cards and costs
prompt: Define numbered_cards(names, costs) using enumerate(zip(...), start=1). Return strings such as "1: Xbow costs 6". Inputs have equal length.
tests:
assert numbered_cards(["Xbow","Knight"],[6,3]) == ["1: Xbow costs 6","2: Knight costs 3"], "pair each card with its cost and number from one"
assert numbered_cards([],[]) == [], "empty inputs produce no lines"
hint: Unpack number, (name, cost) in the loop.
solution:
def numbered_cards(names, costs):
    return [f"{number}: {name} costs {cost}" for number, (name, cost) in enumerate(zip(names, costs), start=1)]

title: Yield losses lazily
prompt: Define loss_rows(rows) as a generator yielding only rows with derived == "LOSS". Example: WIN, LOSS, UNKNOWN yields just LOSS.
tests:
import types
rows = [{"derived":"WIN"},{"derived":"LOSS","ts":"20261029_120000"},{}]
g = loss_rows(rows)
assert isinstance(g,types.GeneratorType), "loss_rows must return a generator"
assert list(g) == [rows[1]], "yield only the recorded loss"
assert list(g) == [], "a consumed generator does not restart itself"
hint: yield hands one value to the caller and pauses the function.

title: Summarise real opponent-card losses
prompt: Define card_losses(path). Read the real JSONL file. For rows with derived == "LOSS" and dry_run is False, count each distinct string in opp_cards once per match. Missing opp_cards means no observed cards. Example: ["Xbow","Xbow"] contributes one Xbow loss.
hint: Use a set to avoid counting repeated sightings of the same card twice in one match.
